root.claim: One deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, refuting the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in this model.
root.method: Build the two accelerated tape procedures (address interchange and simultaneous butterfly layers), use them inside synthetic transforms and Gaussian resampling to compute a convolution, assemble the multiplication algorithm with exact recovery, and total the cost.

motivation.text: A transform-based product scans $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ levels and so costs $n\log n$; a power saving needs cheaper movement and cheaper arithmetic, which the two procedures supply, and everything else is built around them.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

motivation.text: A call at parameter $mf$ makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$ on streams of volume $V/W$, so the normalized cost grows by $s/W<m$ per level, which is a power of the parameter below one.
